verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              ततश्चितां बकपतेः कारयामास राक्षसः । रत्नैर्गन्धैश्च बहुभिर्वस्त्रैश्च समलंकृताम् ॥१॥
verses.english: Having heard these words of Nara and Narayana, the Rishi Narada became filled with devotion towards the Supreme Being. Indeed, with his whole soul he gave himself up to Narayana.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रज्वाल्य नृपतिर्बकराज प्रतापवान् । प्रेतकार्याणि विधिवद्राक्षसेन्द्रश्चकार ह ॥२॥
verses.english: Having lived for a full thousand years in the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, having seen the immutable Hari, and heard the excellent discourse having Narayana for its theme, the celestial Rishi went to his own hermitage on the breast of Himavat.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्काले च सुरभिर्देवी दाक्षायणी शुभा । उपरिष्टात्ततस्तस्य सा बभूव पयस्विनी ॥३॥
verses.english: Those foremost of ascetics, viz., Nara and Narayana, however, continued to live in their charming hermitage of Vadari, practising the severest austerities.

verses.sanskrit: तस्या वक्त्राच्च्युतः फेनः क्षीरमिश्रस्तदाऽनघ । सोऽपतद्वै ततस्तस्यां चितायां राजधर्मणः ॥४॥
verses.english: You are born in the race of the Pandavas. You are of immeasurable energy. O perpetuator of the race of the Pandavas, having listened to this discourse on Narayana from the beginning, you have, in sooth been purged off of all your sins and your soul has been sanctified.

verses.sanskrit: ततः संजीवितस्तेन बकराजस्तदाऽनघ । उत्पत्य च समीयाय विरूपाक्षं बकाधिपः ॥५॥
verses.english: Neither this world nor the next world is for him, O best of kings, who hates instead of loving and respecting the immutable Hari.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽभ्यगाद्देवराजो विरूपाक्षपुरं तदा । प्राह चेदं विरूपाक्षं दिष्ट्या संजीवितस्त्वया ॥६॥
verses.english: The ancestors of that person who hates Narayana, who is the foremost of gods, and is otherwise called Hari, sink into hell for good.

verses.sanskrit: श्रावयामास चेन्द्रस्तं विरूपाक्षं पुरातनम् । यथा शापः पुरा दत्तो ब्रह्मणा राजधर्मणः ॥७॥
verses.english: O foremost of men, Vishnu is the soul of all beings. How, then can Vishnu be heated, for in hating him one would hate his own self.

verses.sanskrit: यदा बकपती राजन् ब्रह्माणं नोपसर्पति । ततो रोषादिदं प्राह खगेन्द्राय पितामहः ॥८॥
verses.english: He who is our preceptor, viz., the Rishi Vyasa, the son of Gandhavati, has himself recited this narrative to us about the glory of Narayana, that glory which is the highest and which is immutable. I heard it from him and have recited it to you exactly as I heard it, O sinless one.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्मूढो मम सभां नागतोऽसौ बकाधमः । तस्माद्वधं स दुष्टात्मा न चिरात्समवाप्स्यति ॥९॥
तदयं तस्य वचनान्निहतो गौतमेन वै । तेनैवामृतसिक्तश्च पुनः सञ्जीवितो बकः ॥१०॥
verses.english: This religion, with its mysteries and its abstract of details, was won by Narada, O king, from that Lord of the universe, viz., Narayana himself.

verses.sanskrit: राजधर्मा बकः प्राह प्रणिपत्य पुरन्दरम् । यदि तेऽनुग्रहकृता मयि बुद्धिः सुरेश्वर ॥११॥
verses.english: Even such are the particulars of this great religion. I have, before this, O foremost of kings, explained it to you in the Hari-Gita, with a brief reference to its ordinances.

verses.sanskrit: सखायं मे सुदयितं गौतमं जीवयेत्युत । तस्य वाक्यं समादाय वासवः पुरुषर्षभ ॥१२॥
verses.english: Know that the Island-born Krishna, otherwise called Vyasa, is Narayana on Earth. Who else than he, O foremost of kings, could compile such a work as the Mahabharata? Who else than that powerful Rishi could describe the diverse kinds of duties and religion for the। observance and adoption of men.

verses.sanskrit: सिक्त्वाऽमृतेन तं विप्रं गौतमं जीवयत्तदा । सभाण्डोपस्करं राजंस्तमासाद्य बकाधिपः ॥१३॥
verses.english: You are bent upon celebrating a great sacrifice. Let that sacrifice of yours be celebrated! Having listened to the various kinds of duties and religions, let your Horsesacrifice go on.

verses.sanskrit: सम्परिष्वज्य सुहृदं प्रीत्या परमया युतः । अथ तं पापकर्माणं राजधर्मा बकाधिपः ॥१४॥
विसर्जयित्वा सधनं प्रविवेश स्वमालयम् । यथोचितं च स बको ययौ ब्रह्मसदस्तथा ॥१५॥
verses.english: Sauti said Having heard this great discourse, that best of kings began all those rites that are laid down in the ordinance, for the completion of his great sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मा चैनं महात्मानमातिथ्येनाभ्यपूजयत् । गौतमश्चापि सम्प्राप्य पुनस्तं शबरालयम् । शूद्रायां जनयामास पुत्रान् दुष्कृतकारिणः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Accosted by you, O Shaunaka, I have duly recounted to you and all these Rishis who inhabit the Naimisha forest, that great discourse having Narayana for theme.

verses.sanskrit: शापश्च सुमहांस्तस्य दत्तः सुरगणैस्तदा । कुक्षौ पुनर्भ्वाः पापोऽयं जनयित्वा चिरात्सुतान् ॥१७॥
verses.english: The Supreme god Narayana is the Lord of all the foremost of Rishis, and of the three worlds. He is the upholder of Earth herself of huge proportions. He is the receptacle of the Shruti's and of the quality of humility. He is the great receptacle of all those ordinances that should be practised for acquiring tranquillity of heart, as also of all those who go by the name of Yama. He is always accompanied by the foremost of twice-born ones. Let that great god be your refuge.

verses.sanskrit: निरयं प्राप्स्यति महत् कृतघ्नोऽयमिति प्रभो । एतत्प्राह पुरा सर्वं नारदो मम भारत ॥१८॥
संस्मृत्य चापि सुमहदाख्यानं भरतर्षभ । मयाऽपि भवते सर्वं यथावदनुवर्णितम् ॥१९॥
verses.english: Hari ever does what is agreeable and beneficial to the dwellers of heaven. He is always the killer of such Asuras. He is the receptacle of penances. He is endued with great fame. He is the killer of the Daityas known by the name of Madhu and Kaitabha. He is the ordainer of the ends that are gained by persons acquainted with and observant of scriptural and other duties. He removes the fears of all persons. He takes the foremost of those offerings which are offered in sacrifices. He is your refuge and protection.

verses.sanskrit: कुतः कृतघ्नस्य यशः कुतः स्थानं कुतः सुखम् । अश्रद्धेयः कृतघ्नो हि कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः ॥२०॥
verses.english: He is endued with attributes. He is endued with four-fold form. He shares the merits originating from the dedication of tanks and the observance of similar religious rites. Undefeated and gifted with great power, it is He who always ordains the end, approachable by the Soul alone, of Rishis of pious deeds.

verses.sanskrit: मित्रद्रोहो न कर्तव्यः पुरुषेण विशेषतः । मित्रध्रुङ्नरकं घोरमनन्तं प्रतिपद्यते ॥२१॥
verses.english: He is the witness of the worlds. He is unborn. He is the one ancient Purusha. Endued with solar complexion, He is the Supreme Lord, and He is the refuge of all. Do all of you bow your heads to Him since He who originated from the water (viz., Narayana himself) bends his head to Him.

verses.sanskrit: कृतज्ञेन सदा भाव्यं मित्रकामेन चैव ह । मित्राच्च लभते सर्वं मित्रात्पूजां लभेत च ॥२२॥
verses.english: He is the origin of the universe. He is that Being who is called Eternal. He is Minute. He is the refuge upon whom all things depend. He is the one Being who is immutable. The Sankhyas and Yogins, of controlled souls, hold him who is eternal in their understanding.

verses.sanskrit: मित्राद्भोगांश्च भुञ्जीत मित्रेणापत्सु मुच्यते । सत्कारैरुत्तमैर्मित्रं पूजयेत विचक्षणः ॥२३॥
verses.english: For friends one may enjoy various objects of life. By the exertions of friends, one may escape from various sorts of danger and distress. He who is wise would honour his friends to the best of his power.

verses.sanskrit: परित्याज्यो बुधैः पापः कृतघ्नो निरपत्रपः । मित्रद्रोही कुलाङ्गारः पापकर्मा नराधमः ॥२४॥
verses.english: An ungrateful, shameless and sinful wretch should be shunned by the wise. One who injures his friends is a despicable character. Such a sinful person is the vilest of men.

verses.sanskrit: एष धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ प्रोक्तः पापो मया तव । मित्रद्रोही कृतघ्नो वै किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥२५॥
verses.english: I have thus told you, O foremost of all virtuous men the characteristics of a sinful wretch who is stained by ingratitude and who injures his friend. What else do you wish to hear.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा तदा वाक्यं भीष्मेणोक्तं महात्मना । युधिष्ठिरः प्रीतमना बभूव जनमेजय ॥२६॥
verses.english: Hearing these words spoken by the great Bhishma, Yudhishthira, O Janamejaya, was highly pleased.
